samples.summary: The `store.delete` branch of `applyBorderPatch` is never asserted at store level — no test proves a style-only cell is removed rather than left as an empty shell
samples.evidence: `applyBorderPatch` (sheet.ts:4152-4157) ends with `if (isEmptyCell(newCell)) await this.store.delete(anchor)`. The only scenario that reaches it is a cell that had ONLY border style and no value — i.e. the 'should clear borders from selected range' test (formatting.test.ts:330-342). That test asserts only `getStyle(...)` is `undefined`, which is equally true if the code stored a `{}`/`{s:{}}` shell instead of deleting. The two tests that DO inspect the store (line 349/414 `fetchGrid(...).get('A1')`, line 366 `fetchGrid(...).size`) use cells that either keep a value (`v: 'Label'`) or never existed, so neither exercises the delete path. Nothing asserts `fetchGrid(...).size === 0` after `all` then `clear` on originally-empty cells — the exact residue the todo doc (docs/tasks/active/20260822-sheets-clear-borders-prune-todo.md:22-24, 38) says the change fixes.
searchedFor: grep setRangeBorders|applyBorderPatch across repo (only formatting.test.ts in tests)
grep for fetchGrid assertions in the new tests

samples.summary: The 'keep spill metadata' test's apply half would pass even if the border write were a complete no-op on spill cells
samples.evidence: Lines 427-437 assert `setRangeBorders('all')` returns true and then use `toMatchObject({f, spillRows, spillCols})` / `toMatchObject({v, spillAnchor})`, which ignore the `s` field entirely — they never assert any border was actually written to the anchor or the ghost. The post-clear assertions (441-449) use `toEqual` with no `s`, which is also satisfied by a cell that never received a style. So the whole test passes if `applyBorderPatch` silently skipped spill cells, i.e. it does not verify borders survive/apply on a dynamic-array range, only that the two direct `store.set` payloads are unchanged. Adding an assertion on the cell's `s` after the 'all' step would make it real coverage.

samples.summary: The pruning change alters every border preset, but `inner`/`top`/`bottom`/`left`/`right` have no test at all
samples.evidence: `toBorderPatchForPreset` emits explicit `false` for `inner` (br/bb hardcoded false, bt/bl false on edge cells) and for `top`/`bottom`/`left`/`right` on non-matching cells (style-mutation.ts:361-375). Those `false` values now take the new prune-or-keep path in `applyBorderPatch`. `rg "setRangeBorders\('(inner|top|bottom|left|right)'\)" packages/sheets/test` returns no matches — only `all`, `outer` and `clear` are exercised anywhere in the suite. E.g. `top` applied to a multi-row selection writes `bt:false` on the interior rows, which now deletes a pre-existing top border there; nothing pins that behavior.
searchedFor: rg setRangeBorders repo-wide (only formatting.test.ts among tests)

samples.summary: The 'keep an explicit false' conflict path is tested only for the column layer; sheet/row/range-style layers are untested
samples.evidence: The doc comment on `applyBorderPatch` (sheet.ts:4109-4110) claims a `false` needed to override a 'sheet/column/row/range-style layer' is still written, and `getStyleSources()` feeds all four layers into `pruneRedundantDefaultStyleKeys`. Only the column case is covered (test at line 369-378, via `selectColumn(1)` + `setRangeStyle({bt:true})`). No test uses a row style, a sheet-wide style, or a `rangeStyles` patch as the conflicting layer, so a regression in three of the four source layers would go unnoticed.

samples.summary: The `stylesEqual` idempotency early-return has no test
samples.evidence: `applyBorderPatch` skips the write when the merged style equals the previous one (sheet.ts:4148-4150). No test in formatting.test.ts applies the same preset twice and observes that no store write / no dirty event occurs, so this optimisation branch is unverified. Low impact since the observable end state is identical either way.

finding.summary: No test covers a cell that carries non-border style when a border preset is applied/cleared
finding.evidence: `applyBorderPatch` (sheet.ts:4009-4020) merges the patch into the existing `cell.s` and then deletes only the patched keys, i.e. it is specifically responsible for PRESERVING unrelated style keys (`b`, `al`, `bg`, ...) across a border apply/clear. Every new and updated test in the diff starts from a cell with either no style at all (lines 272-342, 361-367) or with only a value (`{ v: 'Label' }`, lines 344-359), so no assertion would fail if the merge dropped or clobbered an existing non-border style. A test like `setStyle({b:true})` -> `setRangeBorders('all')` -> `setRangeBorders('clear')` expecting `{b:true}` to survive is absent.

verdict.reason: The finding claims no test covers a cell carrying non-border style across a border apply/clear. Two such tests exist in the exact file cited. formatting.test.ts:380-403 ("should keep non-border style across a border apply and clear") seeds setStyle({b:true, bg:'#ff0000', al:'center'}), runs setRangeBorders('all') asserting the non-border keys survive alongside bt/bl/br/bb, then setRangeBorders('clear') asserting the style is exactly {b:true, bg:'#ff0000', al:'center'} — literally the scenario the reviewer describes as absent. formatting.test.ts:405-416 additionally covers the prune-to-nothing branch: a cell with {v:'Label'} + {b:true} after 'clear' must still be {v:'Label', s:{b:true}}. Both use a real Sheet over a real MemStore with no mocks, and use exact-equality assertions, so they would fail if mergeStylePatch/the delete loop in applyBorderPatch (sheet.ts:4133-4139) dropped or clobbered unrelated style keys. The tests are meaningful, not vacuous.
